thread:
sophia_support: Heads up — acme-prod reported intermittent high tail latency (5–12s) + 429s on /v1/generate. First spike ~2026-02-18 03:20 UTC, repeats ~30m. Dedicated-eu2-pool throttle metric spikes at same time. Anyone?

raj_oncall: I'm on it. Can you paste a sample req id and any trace? Also any autoscale events correlated?

sophia_support: Sample req id rq_e9f3a2c. Trace shows 429 rate_limited token_bucket:0 but our metrics show node label "MIG_saturation" true around the same timestamps. Logs snippet:```[2026-02-18T03:20:12Z] node/node-42: mig_saturation=true sm_util=98% mem_bw=89% throttle_count=7325
[2026-02-18T03:20:13Z] pod/acme-gen-0: 429 -> rate_limited
[2026-02-18T03:20:14Z] pod/acme-gen-1: 502 backend_timeout shared-kv-miss
```

maria_eng: Can you run `kubectl get pods -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated-eu2` and `ssh node-42 sudo nvidia-smi mig -lgci`? Need to see MIG layout and pod device assignment.

noah_infra: I SSH'd in and ran checks. Node-42 (A10) has MIG profiles: 3x 1g.5gb. Device plugin shows two heavy acme pods pinned to the same MIG instance (device 0). dmesg shows repeated 'gpu_throttle' kernel msgs. So contention is likely per-MIG-instance.

maria_eng: If two heavy workloads share the same MIG instance they will contend on SM and memory bandwidth. Our device-plugin should place pods on separate MIG instances but it looks like affinity wasn't respected for these pods (old scheduling constraint).

sophia_support: Customer sent a small repro. They run 8 concurrent requests (~2k tokens each). Repro curl:```curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-mini","input":"x"}' | jq .``` They run this in a loop.

raj_oncall: I checked the cluster-autoscaler events — it scaled +1 node ~2m after the first spike. Our autoscaler rule for this pool triggers on CPU, not GPU SM util. So scaling was too slow.

maria_eng: Two things: 1) add sm_util (or inferred gpu_util) as a scaling metric, 2) enforce strict MIG instance affinity for device-plugin so pods don't pack onto the same MIG instance. Also consider bumping min_replicas for high-variance customers.

noah_infra: Opening infra ticket INF-2026 to add GPU util to autoscaler for dedicated-eu2-pool and to set min_replicas=2 for acme-prod as a temporary mitigation. ETA ~2h for rollout.

sophia_support: Customer asked if temporary bump will affect billing.

finance-bot: @sophia_support Note: Bumped reserved capacity will be billed per contract SLA 4.2. Billing ticket BIL-554 queued for review. :white_check_mark:

acme_ops: We also saw a 502 with 'shared-kv-miss' in traces — could that be related to MIG contention?

maria_eng: Yes — L3/cache and memory bandwidth contention at the physical GPU level can increase KV cache miss rates and stall host-side processing, surfacing as backend timeouts or 502s. Moving pods to separate MIG instances or whole-GPU nodes reduces this.

raj_oncall: Action items: 1) noah -> add sm_util to autoscaler and roll patch 2) maria -> patch device-plugin affinity for this pool + evict/rebind offending pods 3) sophia -> communicate repro timeline and mitigation to customer 4) eng-observability -> add KV cache hit-rate to dashboards.

noah_infra: Patch queued. Deploy-bot: `autoscaler-config-update applied to dedicated-eu2-pool by noah_infra`

sophia_support: Customer confirmed latencies dropped after +1 node and we forced pod affinity. They'll run longer repro overnight and report back. I'll keep thread updated. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: Thanks, seeing much fewer 429s now. Will report if anything else shows up.

maria_eng: We'll monitor KV hit-rate and sm_util over next 24h. If pattern repeats, recommend moving heavy jobs to dedicated whole-GPU (no MIG) for acme.

sophia_support: Closing when stable — follow-ups in INF-2026 and BIL-554. Thanks all.
